clue.text: Ineffectual type, male at sea on amphibious vehicle

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and lost, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of the word male, reworked
the DUKW, or duck, was a wartime amphibious truck

explanation.surface: A useless man seen bobbing around the sea aboard an amphibious craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an idiom for a person or thing that is weak, failing and unable to cope.

clue.text: Sex drive brought on by one breadth in outdoor pool

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool
I is one, B is the abbreviation for breadth

explanation.surface: Desire stirred up by doing a width in an open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the psychological term for sexual desire or appetite.

clue.text: Slander married marshal

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married
to marshal troops is to line them up, align them

explanation.surface: Defaming a military marshal who is married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' reads as a rank but is the verb to arrange in line.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them falsely, which is what slander means.

clue.text: Completely depressed on awful ghetto patrol

indicators.note: awful means very bad, so the next word is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: feeling down is feeling depressed
the six letters of ghetto, rearranged
a guard's patrol is a round

explanation.surface: Feeling utterly low after a grim patrol through a ghetto.
explanation.definitionFit: Down to the ground is an idiom meaning entirely or perfectly, as in 'suits me down to the ground'.

clue.text: Got in touch with editor after meeting

indicators.note: after puts the word preceding it second, behind the word that follows

parts.note: contact is a meeting or coming together
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone reached out to an editor once a meeting was over.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to communicate with or reach them, the past tense matching the clue.

clue.text: Animal from British Columbia in vessel

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
standard abbreviation for the Canadian province

explanation.surface: A creature shipped over from western Canada in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: British Columbia is Canada's westernmost province, where bobcats do live.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a wild North American lynx, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Piece of furniture shown in rare catalogue

parts.note: something occasional happens only rarely
a table is a list or catalogue of data

explanation.surface: An antique piece pictured in a hard-to-find sale catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasional table is a small portable side table used as needed.

clue.text: One Muse? Manage to include each one

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage
each is ALL, and one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Musing on whether one Muse could cope with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Calliope is one example of a Muse, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek Muse of epic poetry, one of the nine.

clue.text: Coach's running shoes

definitions.note: read as 'coach is', a trainer is
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., someone who coaches
second meaning: British word for sports shoes, sneakers

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe hides the plural: 'Coach's' must be heard as coaches, people who train others. In Britain trainers are what Americans call sneakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainers are people who coach athletes, and also the British name for athletic footwear.

clue.text: Refuse all round about

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the sum is the whole, all of it
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone declining an offer that goes round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is worthless matter or rubbish, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Former PM's outright victory

parts.note: a bald statement is plain and outright
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister's landslide at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin served three times as British prime minister between the wars.

clue.text: Racehorse trainer, one standing in front of a girl

parts.note: Sir Henry Cecil was a celebrated British racehorse trainer
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse trainer standing ahead of a young woman, perhaps at a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cecil trained many Derby and Classic winners at Newmarket.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecilia is a girl's given name, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Poke one with end of fat finger

parts.note: a dig is a poke or jab
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the last letter of fat

explanation.surface: Jabbing someone with a chubby finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit is the formal or anatomical word for a finger or toe.

clue.text: Notice by embassy showing entry charge

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A sign at a consulate stating what visitors must pay to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the price paid to enter a venue, as in an admission fee.

clue.text: Mounted policeman, say — dependable person, we hear

parts.note: to state something is to say it

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound and not the meaning

parts.note: a trouper is a reliable, uncomplaining person who keeps going

explanation.surface: Praise for a horseback officer as a steady, reliable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it means 'for example', but it is the verb STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a mounted police officer, and US state troopers descend from that tradition.

clue.text: Slim leg spinner, balding

parts.note: slim and thin are synonyms
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A slender cricketer who bowls leg-spin and is losing his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg spinner is a cricket bowler, but here 'leg' and 'spinner' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin on top is an idiom for losing the hair on one's head.

clue.text: A pest flying around tiny climbing plant

indicators.note: flying suggests scattering in all directions, so the letters are jumbled
around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap the next word

parts.note: the five letters of a pest, rearranged
wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: An insect buzzing round a little plant climbing a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: WEE goes inside the rearranged letters after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a fragrant annual that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: Be unable to find drop of Madeira left in one room

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the wine is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Madeira
the Roman numeral for one
room means space, as in room to move
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Losing track of a last drop of Madeira left in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside SP-ACE, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to lose it by putting it somewhere you cannot remember.

clue.text: Warmth? Ideal, I suspect, for a butterfly

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not right, so the letters before it are out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone musing that warm weather suits a butterfly perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in 'I suspect' does double work as fodder; 'suspect' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The white admiral is a British woodland butterfly, dark with a white band across its wings.

clue.text: Lighter after short time in capital

indicators.note: after sends the word before it to the back, behind the phrase that follows

parts.note: a mo is a moment, informally
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge, as is a scow

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter wanted after a brief stay in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is not the cigarette kind but a barge for unloading ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: The man taken in by right-wing supposition

indicators.note: being taken in by someone means being received inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man fooled by a right-wing conjecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a hypothesis or supposition put forward to explain something.

clue.text: Artificial language used in ten operas, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be put together differently

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A made-up tongue sung in a run of ten operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a constructed international language devised by Zamenhof in the 1880s.

clue.text: English architect using northern wood

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
ash is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: An English architect building with timber from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash designed Regent Street and the Brighton Pavilion in Regency England.

clue.text: Cog, extremely thin? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is dropped and only the other half remains

parts.note: too means excessively, extremely
taken as written, before half is removed

explanation.surface: A wheel's cog worn very thin, with 'Not half!' as the emphatic British reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which disguises its job of cutting the word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A cog is one tooth on a gearwheel, so the two words name the same projection.

clue.text: A trifling sum or what could make up a packet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very small amount of money

definitions.text: what could make up a packet
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the snack nuts sold in bags

explanation.walkthrough: A packet is also slang for a lot of money, so the second half seems to contradict the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a paltry payment and the salted legumes sold in snack bags.

clue.text: Leaves company after explorer returns

indicators.note: after places the word before it second, behind the returned name
returning means going back the way one came, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: John Cabot, Venetian explorer of North America
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a firm once a famous explorer comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun: the dried leaves of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is made from the cured leaves of the tobacco plant.

clue.text: List latest info secured by a DA

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A district attorney holding on to the newest intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Rule about intense backing in sport

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to hold sway is to rule

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: deep feelings are intense ones

explanation.surface: A regulation concerning fierce support in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests support for a team, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway is motorcycle racing on an oval dirt track, a spectator sport.
